checks.name: a file backs what it said it delivered

must.item: Only the woman on the right receives the face from portrait-woman.jpg.
must.why: Only the woman's face changed in both versions. The man's face is untouched in version 1 and redrawn but still his in version 2.

must.item: The bearded man on the left still looks like the same person (small drift from a redrawn photo is acceptable).
must.why: He is clearly the same man. In version 2 his hair and beard are slightly redrawn and the crop is a little different.

must.item: The woman on the right is recognisably the person in portrait-woman.jpg, blended to the beach lighting and head angle.
must.why: Version 2 clearly shows the selfie woman's face and dark curly hair, lit naturally. Version 1 is only weakly recognisable, because the face looks barely changed from the original blonde woman.

must.item: The bodies, clothing, beach background and wide framing look the same at a glance.
must.why: Clothing, beach and sea match. Version 2 is cropped slightly to exact 16:9, so the horizon sits a bit higher, which is minor.
No text appears in either output.

faults.what: Version 1 (face only) shows almost no visible change from the original blonde woman, so the swap is weak and barely recognisable as the user.
Version 2 was redrawn by a full-image AI edit. It is slightly re-cropped (original 640x384 became 640x360) and the man's hair and face texture are slightly altered, with a softer look.
The user wanted a face-and-hair swap, but the agent made two versions and spent extra credits.

summary: Version 2 convincingly puts the user's face and dark curly hair on the woman while keeping the man and the beach almost the same, but version 1 barely changed the face and version 2 is slightly re-cropped and redrawn.
